answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: The numbers match fine-tune bias closely. The raw-score shift is 11.3 ×10⁵ (document: 10.4; every other class is 2.3–3.9). Direction consistency is 0.708 (document: 0.70). The final-layer jump is +0.116, with layer 32 at 0.429 (document: +0.10 and 0.41). The mid-layer size ratio is 1.022, which rules out quantization's shrinkage. KL is 0.080 (document: 0.082). Onset is layer 12 (document: 13–14) and effective rank is 3.15 (document: 3.0). Median first divergence is 8, which rules out both system-prompt classes, and the layer-2 spike of 4.6 is far below their ~40. The late onset and the activation curve with no early bump rule out the fine-tune backdoor (onset 3, consistency 0.62). The text does not show the documented extra refusals (0 added, 1 dropped), but that difference is small on 64 prompts, and the activation and logit fingerprint is decisive.
